hints: Differentiate $x=(\ln t)^2$ by the chain rule and $y=e^{2-t^2}$ by differentiating the exponent.
Substitute $t=e$, use $\ln e=1$, and combine the powers of $e$ before simplifying.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $x = (\ln t)^2$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 2(\ln t) \cdot \dfrac{1}{t} = \dfrac{2\ln t}{t}$$

Differentiate $y = \mathrm{e}^{2 - t^2}$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \mathrm{e}^{2 - t^2} \cdot (-2t) = -2t\mathrm{e}^{2 - t^2}$$

Form the parametric derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{-2t\mathrm{e}^{2 - t^2}}{\dfrac{2\ln t}{t}} = -\dfrac{t^2\mathrm{e}^{2 - t^2}}{\ln t}$$
